cohorts.subjects: Dry vertebrae C3 to L5 removed from ten Chinese cadavers of Singaporean origin; soft tissue trimmed, soaked 30 min in a solution printed as sodium hydrochloride, rinsed, air dried and stored at constant temperature and humidity. Institution of origin, sex, cause of death and inclusion or exclusion criteria (degeneration, osteophytes, fracture, transitional or numerical variants) are not stated. Tables 2 to 4 hold this cohort's Table 1 means set against the cited series as percent differences.
cohorts.n_units: 220 vertebrae (C3 to L5, 22 levels) of 10 cadavers; pedicle length only T1 to L5

cohorts.subjects: No subjects: settings of the procedure (soak and rinse times, the fixation hole's diameter and depth, hits per digitised point, readings per parameter, the 0.1 mm thickness given to the end-plate polygon) and the 5 mm transpedicle screw the Discussion uses as a criterion for pedicle width.

techniques.instrument: direct-contact three-dimensional digitiser with a contact probe, stated accuracy 0.01 mm, calibrated by the maker's procedure and connected to a computer; make and model not named. Each vertebra held by a screw in a 5 mm hole drilled about three-quarters into the body from anterior, the screw in a vice clamp, clay to stop motion (Fig. 2); no repositioning of bone or instrument.
techniques.how: Per vertebra a coordinate frame: origin at the centroid of the upper end-plate (found by polygonising the digitised end-plate and giving it 0.1 mm thickness); the posterior wall of the body is the reference plane, set by digitised points a and b and the average of c and d; x-axis from b to a, z-axis by the right-hand rule (Fig. 3). Each digitised position is the average of ten hits. The profile is traced with the probe into a 3D surface; best-fit planes give linear measures between two marked points and areas from a triangular mesh on the plan view, and angles between two chosen planes on the side view (Fig. 4). Each parameter is the mean of three readings. Parameter definitions as Panjabi et al. (Fig. 1 is Panjabi's drawing), pedicle length after McLain and Zindrick (facet cortex to anterior cortex along the PDIs line), PDIs after Zindrick. Left and right pedicles measured separately. Values reported as mean +/- standard error of the mean, which the paper defines as the SD divided by the sample size.

within_paper: One set of subjects measured by one method: the 220 vertebrae of the 10 cadavers give every value of Table 1, and Tables 2, 3 and 4 and the text's numbers restate or compare those same means (p. 137-145, PDF 1-9). The accuracy tests are on gauges, not on the specimens (p. 138, PDF 2). The three comparison series (Panjabi, Zindrick, McLain) are other studies' subjects and the paper states no overlap with its own. Inference: n is 10 per level (220 = 10 x 22), though the paper never prints n per cell.
